headline: Rocket Lab buys Iridium for $8B to rival Starlink
summary: Rocket Lab acquires Iridium Communications for $8 billion to expand its satellite capacity and compete with SpaceX's Starlink and Amazon's Leo.
details: Rocket Lab, a private spaceflight company, has announced its acquisition of Iridium Communications in a deal worth $8 billion. This move aims to enhance Rocket Lab's satellite capacity and compete with major players like SpaceX's Starlink and Amazon's Leo.

Iridium operates a network of 80 satellites that provide connectivity to remote locations worldwide. The acquisition will give Rocket Lab an immediate foothold in various space-based markets, including direct device communications, internet of things networks, and global positioning services.

The deal is expected to benefit Rocket Lab's military satellite contracts and expand its services to untapped markets. Rocket Lab plans to build upon Iridium's network and pioneer new space-based services for global customers.

headline_marked: Comcast [[splits into two companies]] to protect broadband business
headline: Comcast splits into two companies to protect broadband business
summary: The media conglomerate will spin off NBCUniversal and Sky into a separate entity, aiming to bolster its core connectivity services.
details: Comcast has announced plans to split into two publicly traded companies, separating its NBCUniversal and Sky broadcasting arms. This strategic move aims to safeguard the company's highly profitable broadband and wireless division, which will continue under the "Comcast" name.

The media and entertainment business, collectively branded as "NBCUniversal," will house assets including Sky Media, Universal film and television studios, NBC, Peacock, Bravo, and Telemundo. This division faces increasing competition from industry consolidation and streaming services.

The entire separation process is projected to take approximately one year. Upon completion, Comcast shareholders will hold stakes in both the new Comcast and the newly formed NBCUniversal entity. Current Comcast CEO Brian L. Roberts will remain involved in leadership roles for both companies.

Mike Cavanagh, the current co-CEO, has been appointed to lead NBCUniversal, while Michael Angelakis, formerly Comcast's CFO, will take over as CEO of the new Comcast. This leadership transition is a key part of the restructuring.

"Both companies begin this next chapter from positions of strength," stated Cavanagh. "Comcast will continue to build on its leadership in connectivity, while NBCUniversal, together with Sky, will have the scale, brands, content and financial resources to compete as a premier global media and entertainment company."
